Brian.

Hey, guys.

I'm not sure we understand the question, Andrew, on the.
Would it change anything for us?
We want to sell the company.
We want to do so at the maximum value.
So have they put an offer forward?
They put an offer forward, yes, but it's.
Sorry, it's $2 million.
With a million dollars in cash up front and, sorry, not in cash, sorry, in preferred stock of owner up front.
Right.

Okay.

Right.

Right.

And he hasn't changed that offer.
But what he put on the table was if they tell me what they want or what they would accept as part of a cash upfront deal, what would that look like?
But with a deal value of $2 million?
With a deal value of $2 million, yeah.
Which looks something like a 3X.
It's something like that.
So I totally understand, Richard, that you're going to say flat no again, which is fair enough.
But just my thoughts on it is that, you know, we're five months into the process.

So those two things add quite a lot of risk for a buyer and it reduces the multiple.

It's not putting anybody off at that price.
But they will come in with a lower valuation and offer most likely from there.
This offer is not great.
It's a 3x.

So this is an opportunity to liquidate an asset on the balance sheet, get some cash back into the business and focus on Kobe Day.
So I mean, we have to.
I have to take it seriously.

And so there's A big part of buying into a new business.
And then we have shareholders in the business, in the COVID day brake business who would get, I guess, part of a bit of that new company and permissible note.
I've had bad experiences with permissible notes.
Yeah, it doesn't really mean much, Brian.
I appreciate that.
There's another 200 grand to pay as part of the earn out at the end of the 12 months if you maintain.
I think it's 85% of current revenue.
So I mean it isn't a fantastic offer at all.
I'm aware of that.
But I'm also just saying, look, it is a chance to liquidate it to some degree and it's the only offer that is still on the table to be fair.

There should be buyers out there.
This is a decent business.
It's got some good revenue.

But isn't the preferred option.
It's more work harder and find some more deals out there that will be more acceptable.
I think that would be the request.
Okay, well, I accept that request.
Regarding work harder.
I mean we are actively putting this out to market.
I think the thing is there is somewhere between us working harder and you guys being really realistic on the value.
This isn't the best offer.
I appreciate that.
Actually a lot of it is stupid.
The preferred stock on the stock market, they're on, they're on pink sheets over the counter dollar stock.
So doesn't really mean anything at all.
But what I do think it does give us is a realistic or a close to realistic valuation of the business.
So I mean what, what I would like to see is just, just you.
Think that's a realistic valuation of the business.
It's closer to the.
Well, so Richard spoke.
You said three and a half to four.
We're now that then reversed as part of the whole plan and we stuck with the three and a half to four.
We're now down at 2.7 pounds and now we're seeing $2 million.
No.
So I'm not saying this is a great offer at all, Richard, but what I'm saying is it's closer to a realistic valuation.
I've not moved from that since we've started this conversation.
Particularly obviously I want the best deal for you guys.
I'm not really interested in getting out at a stupidly low multiple either.
But.

But I do believe that by sort of constantly trying to go back out to market at a multiple that is higher, it's not generating the interest that is going to get you the result you guys want, which is to liquidate the asset to move on with Corvidae.
Yeah, Now I understand the point you're making.
So we agreed to relist down from the 7x to 5x.
Yeah.

So I'm not entirely sure why you're coming on strong about.
Well, because we're only going to.
We're probably only going to get this opportunity in September.
You're right.
September comes back a lot stronger.
It's where people are back at their desks.
They're looking to get deals done.
So they're going to look at it again for definite and we will go back out to market at 5x, Chris, if that's what you want.
But I want to get this business sold for you so that you guys can move on.
It is priced too high still.
Not that that won't generate interest.

But the fact is we either get offers that are low like this against where we're priced currently, or we just don't get anybody looking at it at all because it's priced out of what they're willing to pay.
So we could get really good buyers.

For instance, if we went back out to market at four or four and a half, we would get a better, bigger pool of buyers that would see it as a more realistic pricing and are more likely to engage with us and put an offer in.
So I'm going through this process with another company and their process is a bit different.

They produce a list of buyers that.

I mean, that is what is producing the results.

Just it's all the proactive work and come September, surely it's worth another push to go out to those guys.
Revisit of the ones we've spoken to already.
Price.
Five.

More from the strategic point of view.
It's not extraordinarily high.

So those two things, they do knock off some of the value from the 5.
Right.
Not a huge amount necessarily, but they will touch that a little bit.
So I don't think it's ridiculous for us to go back to market in September at 5, but it will shrink the pool a little bit.
That's all I'm saying.

Yeah, 3x roughly.

Yeah.
What do you think?

Yeah.

Down on the price.

Yeah.

So, yeah, it seems to me that although we were pausing it, we've actually had progress in the last week.
Yeah, so we were pausing all of our outbound.

It's pointless.

So.
I was going to say.

Week onwards, week after next.

Yeah.

We've.

Yeah, okay, well that's.

Well, we, we've already.

Yeah, I've never experienced really, where somebody felt they had the upper hand and could really push much harder than what we've already dropped the price.
But I guess the honest answer is I don't know.
I don't know because we don't speak to everybody in depth and sometimes they just start to ghost us as well.
So they might not even come back.
But I would say we've done a decent job at this.
We're good at this.
We get businesses sold well within six months and we just went out, I think, too high a multiple.
But I do believe that this is a good business.
We've had a lot of interest.
It's not like nobody's interested.
I've had discussions with buyers and they like the business.
They like where it is, they like what you're doing and they like it.

So.

Every conversation that we have, we, you know, I really don't feel our hands are tied.

Yeah.
Okay.
Thank you.
All right, so the 1.2 million cash up front is good.
In terms of us.
We can just work out exactly what the backstop looks like.
I mean, it may be that it ends up somewhere close to that and under, but.
But it's good to know what your.
Your number is, and we can just get to work with that.
All right.
See what we can get.
And yeah, September.
Fingers crossed.
This is.
This at the moment.
It is.
Thank you.
All right, Good stuff.
Thank you, guys.
Appreciate your time.
Thanks for hopping on Brian in the heat at the moment.
Thanks, guys.
Cheers.
Cheers, cheers.

summary.overview:
- Meeting experienced connection issues, delaying participation and requiring troubleshooting for Brian Fitzpatrick.
- Onar's revised offer valued at $2 million, structured with $1 million in preferred stock and $200k earnout contingent on revenue retention.
- Current offer lacks cash upfront; potential negotiation for $800k cash identified to reinvest in Corvidae business.
- Business has faced declining revenue and Chris's early departure increases buyer risk perception, complicating sale.
- Listing at 5x multiple with realistic market expectation adjusted to 4-4.5x for this business size and profile.
- New pricing strategy supports a shift to a 4.5x multiple to attract a broader buyer pool and generate interest for September relaunch.
- Optimal market timing for relaunch identified as the second week of September, post-summer holiday activity spike.
- Quanta has reengaged for acquisition, showing interest but with valuation expectations misaligned with £10 million target.
- Active pipeline includes 10-11 signed NDAs from targeted outreach, reflecting ongoing interest despite August slowdown.
- Minimum cash upfront expectation established at £1.2 million as a baseline for all acceptable offers.
summary.short_summary: During the meeting, participants addressed several critical points regarding the business's sale and financial strategies. Onar presented a revised offer valued at $2 million, which includes $1 million in preferred stock and a $200k earnout based on revenue retention. However, the current proposal lacks cash upfront, prompting discussions about negotiating for an $800k cash component to reinvest in the Corvidae business. The business is experiencing declining revenue, and Chris's early departure has heightened buyer risk perception, complicating the sale process. The listing price is set at a 5x multiple, though realistic expectations have been adjusted to a 4-4.5x multiple. A new pricing strategy aims to shift to a 4.5x multiple to attract more buyers, with an optimal relaunch timing identified for the second week of September. Quanta has reengaged for acquisition but has misaligned valuation expectations, while an active pipeline reflects ongoing interest despite a slowdown in August.
